children.name: Project Description
children.reason:
Evaluation of the README file:

project_purpose:
Score (avg): 5.0
[CODING] The README clearly and thoroughly explains the project's purpose and value. It states: "Das vorliegende Projekt ist ein Angebot der Familienregion Bamberg, das berufstätige Eltern bei der Vereinbarkeit von Familie und Beruf unterstützen möchte." It explains that Stadt and Landkreis Bamberg run the site (https://ferienportal-bamberg.de) where "Ferienabenteuer" events can be viewed and booked, and that the system supports parents throughout the registration and booking process as well as regional providers in managing their offers. It further describes the two frontends — "Frontend Buchung" for the public/families (booking, cancelling, managing offers) and "Frontend Verwaltung" for organizers/administrators (managing events, providers, discounts) — and provides screenshots plus an architecture diagram. This gives a clear picture of what the project does and why it is useful.

setup_instructions:
Score (avg): 2.0
[CODING] The README does not contain any actual setup instructions. There are no prerequisites, dependency/version requirements, installation steps, build or run commands, environment variable configuration, database setup, or deployment guidance for the top-level project. It only provides an architecture overview listing three sub-projects (CMS: Keystone 6; Verwaltungs Frontend: Angular; Buchungs Frontend: Angular) with links to their respective README files (`src/backend/README.md`, `src/frontend-verwaltung/README.md`, `src/frontend-buchung/README.md`) and a note that "Dokumentation ist in den einzelnen Unterprojekten im entsprechenden Verzeichnis hinterlegt." While these links may point to setup docs, the top-level README itself does not describe how to install, configure, or run the software, so the score is low (2 rather than 1 only because it does at least point readers to the per-subproject documentation).

info_project_status:
Score (avg): 4.0
[CODING] The README communicates the project's status via a prominent warning block: "Wichtiger Hinweis: In diesem Repository ist ein älterer Softwarestand enthalten. Die Weiterentwicklung sowie der aktuelle Code befinden sich in diesem Repository [https://gitlab.opencode.de/smart-city-bamberg/projekt_ferienportal]." This clearly informs readers that the repository contains an older software state and that active further development/current code lives in another repository. It therefore conveys the status reasonably well. It does not, however, explicitly label the repository as archived/no longer maintained, nor provide version numbers or release/changelog information, which is why it is scored 4 rather than 5.

info_maintainer:
Score (avg): 2.0
[CODING] The README identifies the owning organizations — it states the project is "ein Angebot der Familienregion Bamberg" and that "Stadt und Landkreis Bamberg" offer the homepage — and it lists the funding bodies ("Bundesministerium für Wohnen, Stadtentwicklung und Bauwesen und die Kreditanstalt für Wiederaufbau") with a funding logo. However, it does not describe who specifically maintains the code or contributes to the project: there are no named individual maintainers, no contact information, no contribution guidelines (e.g., how to report issues or submit merge requests), and no governance or contributor information. The mention of organizations is useful context but falls short of describing maintainers and contributors, hence a low score.

children.name: Project Structure
children.reason:
Project structure evaluation:

directory_organization:
Score (avg): 4.0
[CODING] The repository is organized as a monorepo with a clear top-level split into shareable metadata (README.md, publiccode.yml), project-wide documentation (docs/ with Architektur.png, Frontend-Buchung.png, Frontend-Verwaltung.png, KFW.png, Kombilogo_BMWSB_KFW.png, Logo_BMI.jpg) and three technology-specific source trees under src/ (backend, frontend-buchung, frontend-verwaltung). Each subtree follows its stack's conventions: the Keystone/Node backend has keystone.ts, schema.ts, schema.prisma, schema.graphql, migrations/, admin/, views/, extensions/ and email_templates/ exactly where a Keystone project expects them; both Angular apps follow the standard Angular layout (angular.json, tailwind.config.ts, codegen.ts, src/app, src/assets, src/environments, src/index.html, src/main.ts, tsconfig*.json, nginx.conf, Dockerfile, docker-compose*.yml). Weaknesses: there is no tests/ directory or any *.spec.ts file anywhere despite frontend-buchung/tsconfig.spec.json and frontend-verwaltung/tsconfig.spec.json being present, and there are stray artifacts such as src/backend/email_templates/account_deleted_due_to_inactivity copy/ (a duplicated folder containing a space and "copy") as well as three separate per-subproject docs/ folders duplicating content (backend/docs/cms-*.jpg, frontend-buchung/docs/Veranstaltungen.png, frontend-verwaltung/docs/Veranstaltungen.png). These are minor blemishes on an otherwise conventional structure, hence a 4 rather than a 5.

naming_conventions:
Score (avg): 3.0
[CODING] Naming is largely consistent within each technology but not across the repository, and several clear inconsistencies exist. Strengths: Angular files uniformly use kebab-case with type suffixes (care-days.component.ts, cart-info.component.ts, app-routing.module.ts, sites-routing.module.ts, click-outside.directive.ts, image-proxy.pipe.ts, components.module.ts, stores.module.ts); database migrations follow a uniform timestamp_snake_case pattern (e.g. 20231214172005_booking_is_request, 20231116165406_bookings_and_tickets); email templates use consistent snake_case directories (booking_confirmed/, discount_application_rejected/) each with content.html + subject.txt. Problems: (1) mixed casing for TypeScript modules in the backend — camelCase (mailConnection.ts, eventQueue.ts, schemaExtensions.ts, codeGenerator.ts), dot-separated (auth.filters.ts, auth.session.ts), and plain lowercase (auth.ts, keystone.ts, messages.ts, environment.ts); (2) camelCase vs kebab-case inconsistency between the two Angular apps — frontend-buchung/src/app/roleGuard.ts breaks the kebab-case pattern used by every neighbouring file; (3) inconsistent spelling of the same domain concept — waiting_list_ticket_* email template folders vs sendEmailWhenWaitinglistTicketConvertedToBooking.ts vs sendEmailWhenWaitingListTicket... style names, plus the typo/mixed-language identifier sendEmailWhenPasswortResetRequested.ts ("Passwort" German inside an English name); (4) a directory name containing a space and a copy suffix, "account_deleted_due_to_inactivity copy/"; (5) non-uniform asset/document names mixing German and English and conventions — Architektur.png, Veranstaltungen.png, Frontend-Buchung.png next to ferienabenteuer_bamberg_logo.svg, Kombilogo_BMWSB_KFW.png, logo-familienregion.svg. These are individually small but collectively make naming only acceptable.

separation_of_concerns:
Score (avg): 4.0
[CODING] Concerns are generally well separated. Documentation is kept out of source directories at the top level (docs/ plus README.md, publiccode.yml), and each subproject carries its own deploy/config artifacts (Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, docker-compose.override.yml, .gitignore, .gitattributes, nginx.conf, tsconfig*.json, tailwind.config.ts, codegen.ts, graphql.schema.json) rather than polluting src/. Static content is separated from code in both Angular apps (src/assets/files/Ferienabenteuer_Widerruf.pdf, src/assets/images/, src/assets/fonts/). Backend content (email_templates/ HTML/text bodies, migrations/*.sql, schema.graphql/schema.prisma) is cleanly separated from the TypeScript implementation logic. Environment-specific configuration is isolated in src/environments/environment.ts and environment.development.ts. The main gap against the stated criterion is the complete absence of tests: there is no tests/ directory and no spec files anywhere, even though tsconfig.spec.json files exist in both frontends, so the source/tests/config separation is only two-thirds realized. Secondary concerns: documentation images are scattered in four locations (root docs/, backend/docs/, frontend-buchung/docs/, frontend-verwaltung/docs/), and frontend-verwaltung/src/assets/images/Logo.png duplicates backend/assets/Logo.png, blurring where shared brand assets belong.

modularity:
Score (avg): 5.0
[CODING] Modularity is a genuine strength. The backend decomposes by feature and concern: extensions/mutations/ contains one file per GraphQL mutation (bookCartTickets.ts, applyForDiscount.ts, registerPayment.ts, generateInvoice.ts — about 38 distinct capabilities), extensions/queries/ is separate from mutations, extensions/worker/ isolates scheduled jobs (deleteInactiveUsers.ts, markOverdueBookings.ts, markOverdueDiscounts.ts, findFinishedEvents.ts), messaging/handlers/ holds one handler per domain event, and messaging/handlers/mailing/ contains one module per notification (sendEmailWhenBookingCreated.ts, sendEmailWhenDiscountApplicationGranted.ts, sendEmailWhenUserVerifiedAccount.ts, about 25 files) with a shared helpers.ts — a textbook single-responsibility breakdown. The Angular apps mirror this: src/app is split into components/, directives/, pipes/, graphql/ (generated.ts + graphql.module.ts), sites/ (feature pages: account, auth, checkout, events, legal) and stores/ where every feature has its own NgRx slice directory (auth, bookings, checkout, children, custodians, discounts, event, events, invoices, organizers, partners, profile, reservations, seasons) aggregated via stores.module.ts, stores/index.ts and a few cross-cutting effects (toasts.effects.ts, landing-page.effects.ts). Feature modules (components.module.ts, directives.module.ts, pipes.module.ts, landing.module.ts, sites.module.ts, prime.module.ts) keep wiring declarative rather than centralized. Only minor refinements would be needed for a perfect score: the duplicated "account_deleted_due_to_inactivity copy/" template folder, the overloaded messaging/handlers/mailing/ directory (~25 files without sub-grouping), and duplicate GraphQL codegen outputs (generated.ts) committed independently in both frontends.
